First, we find the hyperbolic identity that corresponds to the following double-angle formula for cosine: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

Using Osborn's rule, we get the following double-angle formula for the hyperbolic cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta =2{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta -1
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡2\theta +1).
$$

Letting $\theta =\frac{5x}{3}$, we have

$$
{cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{5x}{3})=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{10x}{3})+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3\pi /10}({cosh}^{2}⁡(\frac{5x}{3})+2)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /10}(\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{10x}{3})+1)+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3\pi /10}(\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\frac{10x}{3})+\frac{5}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{3}{20}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{10x}{3})+\frac{5}{2}x)|}_{0}^{3\pi /10} \\  & =[\frac{3}{20}\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\frac{10\cdot (3\pi /10)}{3})+\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{3\pi }{10}]-[\frac{3}{20}\operatorname{sinh}⁡0+0] \\  & =\frac{3}{20}\,\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\pi )+\frac{3\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
